Before I can draft a solid plan, two decisions matter a lot — VS Code has **no public API** to remove cells from the notebook view without changing the open document, which sits in tension with “non-destructive / no kernel impact.”

**1. How should “hiding” work in the editor?**

- **Collapse** — use `notebook.cell.collapseCellInput` / output commands. View-only, no document dirtying, kernel unchanged; cells stay as collapsed bars.
- **Temporary delete** — same idea as the existing [remove-cell plan](.cursor/plans/remove-cell_cell_hiding_b1d649a4.plan.md): pull cells out of the open editor, restore on save. True “gone from scroll,” but the open model changes and Run All skips those cells while hidden.
- **UI-only** — filter tags tree / outline (+ optional dimming); do not change the notebook editor layout.

**2. When a filter is active, which cells get hidden?**

- **Show matches** — hide/collapse non-matching cells (focus filter).
- **Hide matches** — hide/collapse cells that match (factor-out / exclude tags).
- **Both** — Include / Exclude toggle when setting the filter.

Also useful: what’s in scope for “other criteria” beyond tags for v1 (e.g. cell kind, has outputs, executed/not)? If you don’t care, I’ll default to **tags only** for the first cut.

Reply with your choices (e.g. “collapse + both modes + tags only”) and I’ll produce the implementation plan.

---

_**User**_

1. Collapse 
2. Show matches
3. tags, cell kind, has outputs, executed/not

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
A plan is forming around three features. Collapse non-matching cells via commands. Expand matching cells and collapse others. Support filtering by tags, cell kind, outputs, and execution status.

Filter state lives only in extension memory and never touches notebook metadata. Collapsed cells must be tracked separately from user-collapsed ones so clearing the filter can restore them. The filter re-applies automatically when the notebook changes while active. A multi-select quick pick will let users build criteria. Default logic will combine multiple criteria with AND across types and OR within tags.

The collapse command will hide both cell inputs and outputs for non-matching cells. Criteria will be grouped by type, with AND connecting different groups and OR within tags.

Matching cells will expand to stand out. Snapshotting collapse state before applying the filter is ideal, but the VS Code API does not expose whether a cell input is currently collapsed. This prevents a clean restore when the filter is cleared.

The chosen approach tracks which cells were collapsed during the filter. Clearing the filter will expand only those cells. Matching cells will expand to stand out. The filter will recompute when the document changes.

Three commands will handle the filter: set, clear, and internal reapply. The toolbar will show a filter icon that switches to a filled icon when active, driven by a context key. A status bar item will display the current match count. The implementation will live under `src/notebookFilter/`.
</details></think>

{
  "name": "Notebook collapse filter",
  "overview": "Add a view-only notebook focus filter that collapses non-matching cells via collapse commands (no document edits, no kernel impact). Matching uses tags, cell kind, has-outputs, and executed/not; clear expands cells the filter collapsed.",
  "plan": "# Notebook Collapse Filter (Show Matches)\n\n## Decisions locked in\n\n- **Hide mechanism:** collapse non-matching cell inputs (and outputs when present) via `notebook.cell.collapseCellInput` / `collapseCellOutput` — same arg shape as existing execute calls in [`src/notebookRunGroups/util/cellActionHelpers.ts`](src/notebookRunGroups/util/cellActionHelpers.ts) and Jupyter’s own usage: `{ document: uri, ranges: [{ start, end }] }`.\n- **Semantics:** show matches — expand matching cells, collapse the rest.\n- **Criteria (v1):** tags, cell kind, has outputs, executed/not.\n- **Hard constraints:** never call `NotebookEdit` / `WorkspaceEdit` for this feature; never write cell/notebook metadata; filter state lives only in extension memory.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  SetFilter[Set Filter QuickPick] --\u003e Eval[Evaluate each cell]\n  Eval --\u003e|match| Expand[expandCellInput/Output]\n  Eval --\u003e|no match| Collapse[collapseCellInput/Output]\n  Clear[Clear Filter] --\u003e Restore[expand cells we collapsed]\n```\n\n## Matching model\n\nNew types in `src/notebookFilter/filterCriteria.ts`:\n\n```ts\ntype NotebookFilterCriteria = {\n  tags?: string[];           // if set/non-empty: cell must have ANY selected tag\n  cellKind?: 'code' | 'markup';\n  hasOutputs?: boolean;      // code cells: outputs.length \u003e 0; markup treated as false\n  executed?: boolean;        // true if executionSummary.executionOrder != null OR timing/success present\n};\n```\n\n- Criteria fields that are unset are ignored.\n- **AND** across field types; **OR** within `tags`.\n- A filter is “active” when at least one field is set.\n- Tag reads reuse [`getCellTags()`](src/helper.ts). Executed/outputs mirror patterns already used in [`src/cellExecution/cellExecutionTracking.ts`](src/cellExecution/cellExecutionTracking.ts) / [`src/exportExecutedCode/exportExecutedCode.ts`](src/exportExecutedCode/exportExecutedCode.ts).\n\n## Core module: `src/notebookFilter/`\n\n| File | Role |\n|------|------|\n| `filterCriteria.ts` | Types + `cellMatchesFilter(cell, criteria)` |\n| `collapseCommands.ts` | Thin wrappers around collapse/expand input+output for index lists (batch contiguous ranges where helpful) |\n| `NotebookFilterManager.ts` | Per-notebook URI state: active criteria, set of indices we collapsed, apply/clear/reapply |\n| `filterQuickPick.ts` | Multi-step QuickPick UX to build criteria |\n| `startup.ts` | Commands, context keys, listeners, toolbar wiring |\n\n**`NotebookFilterManager.apply(notebook)`**\n\n1. For each cell, evaluate `cellMatchesFilter`.\n2. Non-matches → collapse input; if `outputs.length \u003e 0`, collapse output. Record those indices in `collapsedByFilter`.\n3. Matches → expand input (and output if present) so the focused set is readable.\n4. Set context `jupyter-cell-tags.notebookFilter.active` and optional count key for UI.\n\n**`clear(notebook)`**\n\n1. Expand input/output only for indices in `collapsedByFilter` (avoid `expandAll*`, which would wipe user collapses unrelated to the filter).\n2. Clear criteria + tracking; update context keys.\n\n**Reapply**\n\n- Debounced (~150ms, same pattern as other modules) on `onDidChangeNotebookDocument` while filter is active (tags/outputs/execution may change membership).\n- On `onDidChangeActiveNotebookEditor`, re-sync context keys; filter is per-notebook URI so switching notebooks keeps each notebook’s filter independently.\n\nNo save hooks — collapse is view-state only and does not dirty the document when driven by commands (unlike metadata `inputCollapsed`).\n\n## UX\n\n**Commands** (contribute in [`package.json`](package.json)):\n\n- `jupyter-cell-tags.notebookFilter.set` — “Filter Notebook Cells…”\n- `jupyter-cell-tags.notebookFilter.clear` — “Clear Notebook Cell Filter” (`when`: filter active)\n\n**QuickPick flow** (`filterQuickPick.ts`):\n\n1. Multi-select tags from `getAllTagsFromActiveNotebook()` ([`src/util/notebookSelection.ts`](src/util/notebookSelection.ts)); allow skip (no tag constraint).\n2. Cell kind: Code / Markdown / Any.\n3. Has outputs: Yes / No / Any.\n4. Executed: Yes / No / Any.\n5. Apply; show brief status message e.g. `Showing 12/40 cells`.\n\n**Toolbar** — add to existing `notebook/toolbar` group `navigation/execute@9` (after git-diff):\n\n- Filter icon when inactive → runs `set`\n- Clear / filled-filter icon when `jupyter-cell-tags.notebookFilter.active` → runs `clear`\n\n**Status bar** (lightweight, optional but useful): when active, show `$(filter) N/M` with tooltip summarizing criteria; click clears or reopens set.\n\n## Activation\n\nIn [`src/extension.ts`](src/extension.ts), call `activateNotebookFilter(context)` next to other feature startups.\n\nActivation event: `onCommand:jupyter-cell-tags.notebookFilter.set` plus existing notebook activation paths already covering open notebooks.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Temporary `deleteCells` / remove-cell save-restore (contradicts non-destructive + kernel constraints).\n- Writing collapse state into cell metadata.\n- Exclude/factor-out mode (can add later as a criteria `mode` flag).\n- Filtering side trees (outline already has its own text filter).\n\n## Verification\n\n- Open a notebook with mixed tags/kinds; set filter by tag → non-matching cells collapse, matches expand; document stays clean (not dirty from filter alone).\n- Clear → previously filter-collapsed cells expand; unrelated user collapses left alone as much as possible.\n- Change a cell’s tags while filter active → membership updates after debounce.\n- Run a collapsed non-match via run-group/command still works (cells remain in the model/kernel).\n",

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user's question concerns a launch configuration with type extensionHost. The answer needs to address whether this task can run against VS Code's extension host rather than Cursor's.

F5 with `type: "extensionHost"` from Cursor uses Cursor's own host, so `runtimeExecutable` is typically ignored. To run tests against VS Code's extension host specifically, use `@vscode/test-electron` with a downloaded `Code.exe`. Alternatively, open the project in VS Code for F5, or spawn `Code.exe` with `--extensionDevelopmentPath` through a compound task, though this sacrifices easy debugger attachment.
</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

**Short answer:** Not reliably via F5’s `extensionHost` launch from Cursor. That debug type attaches to **the host you’re running in**, so F5 from Cursor opens a Cursor Extension Development Host. `${execPath}` / `runtimeExecutable` generally won’t switch you to `Code.exe` (and VS Code has treated custom `runtimeExecutable` for `extensionHost` as ignored/broken).

### What works

| Goal | Approach |
|------|----------|
| **F5 + breakpoints against VS Code** | Open the same folder in **Code.exe** and press F5 there (edit in Cursor if you want; debug in VS Code). |
| **Automated extension tests on Code.exe** | Yes — use `@vscode/test-electron` / `vscode-test`. That downloads or points at a real VS Code build and runs `Code.exe` with `--extensionDevelopmentPath` / `--extensionTestsPath`, independent of Cursor. |
| **Manual “run under Code” from Cursor** | A **task** (or script) that starts VS Code with your args, e.g. full path to `Code.exe` + `--extensionDevelopmentPath=${workspaceFolder}` + workspace. That launches VS Code, but Cursor won’t own the debugger unless you set up a more advanced attach flow. |

Example task-style launch (run under VS Code, not Cursor’s host):

```json
"Code.exe" --extensionDevelopmentPath="C:\...\vscode-jupyter-cell-tags" --enable-proposed-api=phohale.pho-vscode-jupyter-cell-tags "C:\...\examples\extension_test_examples.code-workspace"
```

Use the real install path (often under `%LocalAppData%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe`).

### Your current config

Your [`.vscode/launch.json`](.vscode/launch.json) has `"type": "extensionHost"` and no `runtimeExecutable`. From Cursor, that will keep launching **Cursor**. Adding `"runtimeExecutable": "C:\\...\\Code.exe"` is unlikely to give you a proper VS Code Extension Development Host with Cursor debugging.

### Practical setup

- **Day-to-day:** develop in Cursor; for F5/debug against real VS Code APIs (and fewer Cursor-only proposal quirks), F5 from **VS Code**.
- **CI / `npm test`:** target Code via `@vscode/test-electron` so tests never depend on Cursor.

If you meant “task” as in `tasks.json` vs the F5 launch config, say which — a task can start `Code.exe`; it still won’t replace Cursor’s extension-host debugger attachment.
